Find the measure of angle $B$ given that $m∠A=m∠C.$
question.worked_solution:
Using $m∠A=m∠C,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & =m∠C \\ 3z+{20}^{∘} & =4z \\ z & ={20}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, substituting $z={20}^{∘}$ in the expression for $m∠C,$ we get

$$
m∠C=4({20}^{∘})={80}^{∘}.
$$

Now, we can find $m∠B$ using the fact that the internal angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠B+2m∠C & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠B+2\cdot {80}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠B+{160}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠B & ={20}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
